Shells, lithic flakes, potsherds, hammerstones, ochre, and a stone anvil were recovered from four stratigraphic layers. Leang Sarru has four main occupation phases: c. 35,000-31,000 BP (1st phase, Layer 3) with stone tools and shells, c. 22,000-17,000 BP (2nd phase, Layer 2B) with more intensive habitation and the bulk of lithic production, c. 10,000-8,000 BP (3rd phase, Layer 2A), and no habitation after 8,000 BP until reoccupation during c. 2,000-1,000 BP (Metal Age). Layer 1 (Metal Age) contains potsherds similar to jars associated with the Metal Phase (Bellwood, 1976), also found in Leang Buiduane, about 20 km north of Leang Sarru (Tanudirjo, 2001, 2005, Ono et al., 2010).
